# Ad click tokens and fraud checks

> `GET /ads/click/:token` checks a signed ad click token, filters fraud with Redis, always redirects the user to the product, and publishes the click to Kafka.

_Part of [domain/marketing](../../units/domain/marketing.md)_

When `GET /ads/sponsored` serves an ad, `AdsService.sponsored` makes a click token for it. The token holds the impression id, campaign, shop, product and an expiry 30 minutes ahead. It is signed with an HMAC (a keyed hash). The ad's `clickUrl` points at `/api/ads/click/<token>`. Because the token is signed, nobody can forge a campaign id. Because it is tied to an impression, each impression can be billed only once. See [Signed click token with 30-minute expiry](click-token.md). When the user clicks, `AdsController.click` hands the token and the client IP to `AdsService.click`. The IP comes from the `cf-connecting-ip` header, or from `req.ip` if that header is missing. The service checks the signature and expiry. It then runs the fraud checks in order: [One-click-per-impression check in Redis](impression-dedupe.md), then [Per-IP burst limit of 20 clicks a minute](ip-burst-filter.md). It publishes the result to Kafka ([Publishing salted click records to Kafka](click-publishing.md)) and, if the click is valid, adds the campaign's cost per click to the day's spend counter in Redis. The user is always redirected with a 302 to the front-end product page, even if the token is bad, expired, duplicated or flagged as fraud. A bad token goes to `/`. A fraud-filtered click still lands on the product but is not billed. The response is `no-store` so every click reaches the server. Later billing is covered in [Aggregating and billing ad clicks](ad-click-aggregation-and-billing.md), and serving in [Sponsored ad campaigns and serving](sponsored-ad-campaigns.md).

**Look at:** [click-token.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/domain/click-token.ts) · [ads.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/ads.service.ts) · [ads.controller.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/api/ads.controller.ts)

## Pieces

- [Signed click token with 30-minute expiry](click-token.md): A base64url JSON payload plus a truncated HMAC-SHA256 signature, checked in constant time and rejected once expired.
- [One-click-per-impression check in Redis](impression-dedupe.md): A Redis `SET NX` on `adclick:<impression id>` with a 1-hour expiry means a repeat click on the same impression is not counted.
- [Per-IP burst limit of 20 clicks a minute](ip-burst-filter.md): A salted hash of the IP is counted per minute in Redis, and clicks over 20 are marked not valid but still recorded.
- [Publishing salted click records to Kafka](click-publishing.md): Each click is sent to `ads.clicks` with a key of campaign id plus a random salt from 0 to 9, so a viral ad does not overload one partition.
- Click endpoint that always redirects: The controller skips the throttle, sets `no-store` and sends a 302 to the front-end host whatever the result.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| cache | `adclick:<impressionId>` | Set with NX and a 1-hour expiry to dedupe clicks per impression. |
| cache | `adclick:ip:<ipHash>:<minute>` | Counter incremented per click, expiring after 120 seconds, used for the burst limit. |
| cache | `adspend:{<campaignId>}:<day>` | Daily spend counter. A valid click adds the campaign's `cpcCents` to it, and it expires after 2 days. `sponsored` reads it to check budgets. |
| queue | `ads.clicks` | Kafka topic that receives a click record with `click_id`, `campaign_id`, `shop_id`, `ts`, `ip_hash` and `valid`. |
| database | `AdCampaign` | Read for `cpcCents` of the clicked campaign when the click is valid. |

## Also relies on

- [Sponsored ad campaigns and serving](sponsored-ad-campaigns.md): Campaigns and the shared daily spend counter, which `sponsored` also issues tokens against.

## Watch out

- Every outcome is a redirect. A forged, expired or duplicate token still returns a 302, so a redirect does not mean the click was counted or billed.
- A fraud-filtered click is still published to Kafka, with `valid` set to 0. Downstream consumers must check `valid`.
- The signature is cut to 32 characters, and the signing secret is `share_link_secret` with a fallback to `jwt_secret`. The same secret also salts the IP hash.
- The IP burst counter runs only after the dedupe check passes, so repeat clicks on one impression do not count toward the burst limit.
